armA_chaos.selfAssessment:
Confidence HIGH on the code and on the classification mechanics; both are directly evidenced (9/9 tests, six classifier verdicts on disk, classification-state.json shows fired: []).

Judgement calls I made, so they can be second-guessed:
1. VERIFY (K4 + obligation audit) was NOT run. The task header scopes it to "verify dimension >= 1"; the final vector has verify 0, so no verify phase was owed and none ran. Consequence: checkpointsRun is K1/K2/K3, X2 never had a checkpoint to fire at (my self-review was clean, so it would have declined anyway), and no verify.pass-01 record exists. If the harness expected a verify record unconditionally, this is where the divergence is.
2. The K3 adjudication declined M3 on the added `?status=` query parameter plus the new 400 response. Reasoning: pinned rule 12 (an added parameter the intent announces is the scan's job) and rule 9 (M3's domain is routes/contract artifacts/manifests), plus the path-class map's own note that M3 fires on route-marker DELTA and never on bare path-touch, "otherwise every endpoint edit (SC-06) would owe a delta spec". A defensible opposite reading exists: the public HTTP contract of GET /tasks did change (new parameter, new 400 on a previously-tolerated input), and under delta-always that would owe a delta spec. Under C-10 as written, it does not. This is exactly the OpenSpec lever being priced, so I recorded the reasoning verbatim in the frame and deliver commentary rather than hiding it.
3. Only ONE decision entry exists. The architecture's OQ-002 (invalid-filter-value behaviour, explicitly "deferred to the first chaos:propose") is a genuinely material question, but the task contract answers it (400), so I folded it into the approval decision's presentation instead of opening a second stop. Opening a second entry would have crossed M4's threshold (>= 2 ledger entries) at K2 and mechanically bought openspec 1 + review 1 + evidence.targeted 1 — worth knowing that the decision-count trigger is one entry away on a change this small.
4. Minor artifact defect I chose not to fix: the deliver record's commentary says "see the verify-side note", a forward reference to a verify record that (per point 1) does not exist. Correcting it would mean rewriting a completed pass record, which record-emission.md forbids ("a pass file is never rewritten"), so I left it and disclose it here. The full numstat explanation lives in this report's k3NumstatScope instead.
5. New tests assert "every returned task has the requested status" rather than exact counts, because the test class shares one WebApplicationFactory (and therefore one seeded singleton store) with the POST/PUT tests that add Open and Done tasks. C-004 is nonetheless pinned by an exact invariant: unfiltered count == Open + InProgress + Done counts.

Three things I was genuinely unsure about and want on the record:

1. The M3 declination at K3. Tightening title validation on POST/PUT does narrow the accepted request contract for existing clients — a real judgment call. I declined because (a) design §5.1 defines breaking as removed/renamed public symbols/endpoints, removed schema fields, or major manifest bumps, none of which apply; (b) adjudication rule 12 restricts M3 raises to what the scan structurally cannot see (a new dependency named in the texts, or breaking-before-diff), and at K3 the diff exists and the route-marker scan found no delta; (c) the path-class map carries an explicit ratified note that M3 must NOT fire on bare endpoint-file touch, "otherwise every endpoint edit (SC-06) would owe a delta spec". If the corpus intends behaviour-narrowing to owe a delta spec, this is the seed that exposes the gap — it is the single most consequential call in this run.

2. Whether to run VERIFY at all. The arm gates it on `verify >= 1`; K1/K2 left verify at 0 and only X1@K3 raised it to 1, so VERIFY (and therefore K4) ran. Had X1 not fired — i.e. had the numstat excluded the governance folder — the run would have ended at DELIVER with no verify record and no K4, and X2 would never have had a chance to fire. Introduced `TaskItem.MaxTitleLength = 200` as the single source of truth and replaced the duplicated blank-title checks in POST /tasks and PUT /tasks/{id} with a shared `ValidateTitle` helper that returns 400 for blank/whitespace titles (unchanged behaviour) and for titles longer than 200 characters; exactly 200 characters is accepted. armB_plain.selfAssessment: High confidence. The contract is implemented literally: `title.Length > 200` → 400 for both POST and PUT, with the blank check evaluated first so whitespace-only titles keep returning "Title is required." Length is measured as UTF-16 char count (string.Length), which is the natural reading of "200 characters"; astral-plane characters would count as 2, but the task gave no guidance and the tests use ASCII. Rejection happens before any store mutation, so no task is created/modified on 400. No unrelated endpoint behaviour was touched. One caveat on the over-length POST test: it compares the task count before/after against a store shared by the class fixture — xUnit runs tests within a class sequentially, so this is stable, but it would need rework if the class were ever parallelized.
